entry_point.discipline_context: Use potential energy, equilibrium, curvature, and numerical relaxation as bounded engineering contexts.
entry_point.rationale: The learner knows calculus, vectors, matrices, eigenvalues, and Python but not formal convex optimisation.
entry_point.analogy_boundary: An objective is not necessarily physical energy, and an iteration is not necessarily physical time evolution.

chapter_sequence.title: Optimisation, stationarity, and curvature
chapter_sequence.purpose: Establish unconstrained objectives and local tests.

chapter_sequence.title: Smoothness, convexity, and conditioning
chapter_sequence.purpose: Build the global geometry used by convergence results.

chapter_sequence.title: Gradient descent and step selection
chapter_sequence.purpose: Define standard and line-search gradient updates.

chapter_sequence.title: Convergence of gradient descent
chapter_sequence.purpose: State convex and strongly convex rates with assumptions.

chapter_sequence.title: Momentum and acceleration
chapter_sequence.purpose: Compare Heavy Ball and the specified NAG recurrence.

chapter_sequence.title: Stochastic objectives and step schedules
chapter_sequence.purpose: Explain stochastic gradients, variance, error floors, and Robbins-Monro conditions.

chapter_sequence.title: Newton's model and local convergence
chapter_sequence.purpose: Connect curvature models to linear-system steps.

chapter_sequence.title: BFGS and quasi-Newton curvature
chapter_sequence.purpose: Explain secant information, inverse-Hessian updates, and line search.

chapter_sequence.title: From equations to Python
chapter_sequence.purpose: Relate a mathematical update to array operations before assessment.

chapter_sequence.title: Exercises and worked solutions
chapter_sequence.purpose: Consolidate scope, calculation, and implementation diagnosis.

implementation_strategy: Use equation-to-array bridges and two executable scalar/vector examples; keep algorithmic assumptions adjacent to their results.
assessment_strategy: End with exactly three worked exercises: theorem scope, deterministic hand calculation, and code diagnosis.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Select the correct theorem scope for stationarity, strong convexity, and convergence.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Interpret assumptions for an equilibrium-like numerical model without equating the objective to energy.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Compute a gradient-descent step and objective gap from a quadratic model.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Use a two-coordinate quadratic as a local curvature model.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Diagnose a sign error in a Python gradient update and verify the corrected iteration.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Diagnose a scalar numerical relaxation update.
